criteria.fail_examples: Annualising a few days as if it were a yearly law

criteria.description: Required journal fields or workings are present so a reviewer can recompute
criteria.objective_evidence: The listed workings, screenshots of public inputs, or journal fields named in the exercise
criteria.fail_examples: A conclusion without arithmetic; missing inputs; 'I made money so it is correct'

criteria.description: Results are complete, net of stated costs, and labelled paper
criteria.objective_evidence: A written statement that lists the period, the paper label, costs included, and any omitted trades
criteria.fail_examples: Reporting only winners; omitting costs; mixing paper and live; calling the result proof of skill

tts.m18.scale: 0-3 per criterion (0 absent, 1 inconsistent, 2 consistent with objective evidence, 3 consistent with clear worked evidence). Paper-only. Profit or a positive paper P&L is not a pass criterion.
tts.m18.pass_default: Proposed configurable default: mean score at least 2.0, no criterion at 0, and no unremediated critical mistake. Self-declared profit does not pass a failed process or maths criterion.
tts.m18.retry: If any critical process or risk-arithmetic criterion scores 0, or if a listed critical mistake appears, mark remediation required even if the quiz passed. The learner resubmits the missing objective evidence (corrected workings, journal fields, or a documented no-trade decision) before the practical can pass. Configurable product default, not an owner-made law and not accreditation.

criteria.description: Shares = risk / (entry - stop) or the stated ATR rule, recomputed correctly
criteria.objective_evidence: Account, risk %, entry, stop or ATR multiple, and resulting size
criteria.fail_examples: Sizing from notional percentage alone; placing the stop after the fill

criteria.description: Positions are grouped by shared driver and group caps are checked
criteria.objective_evidence: A written grouping and the sum of open risk in each group versus the cap
criteria.fail_examples: Counting five correlated names as five independent bets

criteria.description: Gap, liquidity or VaR/ES stress is shown, with explicit no-guarantee language
criteria.objective_evidence: A stressed loss using a gap multiple and/or a stated VaR/ES sample rule, plus a sentence that neither caps future drawdown
criteria.fail_examples: Treating VaR or a stop as a maximum-loss guarantee

criteria.description: The policy states when new risk is not taken
criteria.objective_evidence: Written halt or no-trade conditions (heat, ladder, event, unverified news)
criteria.fail_examples: Adding size to recover after the ladder is hit

criteria.description: Size calculation correct and within the written rule
criteria.objective_evidence: Workings for each sampled trade
criteria.fail_examples: Size above the risk rule

criteria.description: Correlated exposure is grouped and capped
criteria.objective_evidence: Group list and cap check
criteria.fail_examples: Treating correlated names as independent

criteria.description: Drawdown ladder and no-trade gates are followed
criteria.objective_evidence: Account path versus the written rungs, including any no-trade days
criteria.fail_examples: Trading through a halt; revenge sizing

criteria.description: Gaps and events are stress-tested
criteria.objective_evidence: Event calendar checks and a gap multiple on overnight or event trades
criteria.fail_examples: Holding leverage into an unplanned binary event

criteria.description: Arrival versus fill and costs are recorded
criteria.objective_evidence: Journal fields for arrival, fill and itemised costs
criteria.fail_examples: Mid-price reporting presented as a fill

criteria.description: Stops are set before entry and not widened
criteria.objective_evidence: Pre-trade stop in the journal matching the working
criteria.fail_examples: Moving a stop further from entry after entry

criteria.description: Losing-streak, revenge, overconfidence and no-trade rules are evidenced
criteria.objective_evidence: A written precommitment and journal notes when a gate fired, including strategic no-trading
criteria.fail_examples: No psychology process; a revenge trade after a loss streak

criteria.description: Uploaded or AI-proposed rules are restated, paper-tested and never bypass rails
criteria.objective_evidence: A paraphrase of what the AI understood, a paper-test note, and a reject/approve status that preserves risk limits
criteria.fail_examples: Enabling a prompt that says to ignore stops or size up to recover

criteria.description: Human-school evidence is not substituted for AI-strategy approval or the reverse
criteria.objective_evidence: Separate labels on the capstone journal versus any uploaded-strategy result
criteria.fail_examples: Using a quiz score to approve an upload, or a backtest to complete the school

criteria.description: The best argument against each trade is stated
criteria.objective_evidence: A counter-evidence field on sampled journals
criteria.fail_examples: Empty counter-evidence fields

criteria.description: Decision quality is separated from outcome
criteria.objective_evidence: A review that discusses rule adherence independently of P&L
criteria.fail_examples: Judging the plan solely by whether the sample made money

criteria.description: Rules were fixed before the tested sample where claimed
criteria.objective_evidence: A dated plan or parameter freeze
criteria.fail_examples: Changing rules after seeing the result and presenting them as prior

criteria.description: Net, complete, paper-labelled reporting with no accreditation claim
criteria.objective_evidence: A final statement that completion is general education, not a qualification, profit guarantee, or live-competence certificate
criteria.fail_examples: Presenting paper marks as live skill or as industry accreditation
